sources.title: The Green Book: appraisal and evaluation in central government (2026 edition), section 'Discounting'
sources.series_identifier: Social time preference rate (STPR); see also the Green Book supplementary guidance on discounting referenced in the text
sources.locator: Section 'Discounting' (HTML capture, character range ~89,600-91,300 of the captured DOM text); Table 8 'Discounting and present values'
sources.quote: It is set at 3.00% in real terms for years 1 to 30 of an appraisal.
sources.supports: the social lower-bound discount rate and the declining-rate regime (2.50% years 31-75, 2.25% from year 76); also the rule that a real rate must be applied only to real values
sources.limits: A social welfare rate for public-sector appraisal, not a private investor's cost of capital; the page also refers to a separate supplementary guidance document that was NOT read here

sources.title: The Green Book (2026), section 'Discounting' - real-terms requirement
sources.locator: Same 'Discounting' section, paragraph beginning 'Discounting is distinct from adjusting for inflation'
sources.quote: The STPR is a real discount rate and must be applied only to values expressed in real terms
sources.supports: the convention to deflate first and then discount with a real rate; never add inflation to the discount rate

sources.publisher: HM Treasury (GOV.UK), Green Book Discount Rate Review 2026
sources.title: Review of discounting in the Green Book: Terms of Reference (updated 28 October 2026)
sources.series_identifier: STPR parameters delta 0.5%, L 1%, mu 1, g 2% giving 3.5%; SOC alternative
sources.locator: Section 1 'Discounting in the Green Book' and Section 3 'Scope'
sources.quote: The STPR is currently set at 3.5% in real terms for the first 30 years of a proposal.
sources.supports: the conflict with the 2026 Green Book edition (3.00% vs 3.5%) and the description of the abandoned social opportunity cost of capital approach, showing that private-sector returns are a different concept from the social rate
sources.limits: The page states 3.5% as current while the 2026 Green Book edition states 3.00%; both were read on the same day and the conflict is left unresolved rather than reconciled by preference

sources.publisher: HM Treasury (GOV.UK), Green Book Discount Rate Review 2026
sources.title: Review of discounting in the Green Book: Terms of Reference - social opportunity cost of capital
sources.locator: Section 1, final paragraph on the social opportunity cost of capital
sources.quote: This is based on the rate of return that would be expected on funds left in the private sector
sources.supports: the distinction used throughout REPORT.md: a social rate and a private required return are different objects, so the Green Book cannot supply this client's cost of capital
sources.limits: Descriptive of a historical approach; no numeric private hurdle rate is given in the document
